Senses.PreferredTarget: the eye at the crown of the head
AlternateTargets: the eye at the top of the head
Senses.Explanation: Literally, this is an eye at the crown-gate, the top of the head. The records use it with the verbs possess, open, look, illuminate, and strike blind, and with the adjective correct. Lushan Fazhen says that to understand the upward matter one must possess the crown-gate eye; possessing it accords with the heart of leaving home, and he then asks, “do you want to understand the crown-gate eye?” before saying that people in the four capitals put on clothes and eat while people in the two Zhejiang circuits are full and warm (欲明向上事，須具頂門眼；要會頂門眼麼？四京人著衣喫飯，兩浙人飽暖自如). Yuanwu invites “those who possess the crown-gate eye” to raise Xuansha's case (具頂門眼者，請試舉看), and says in verse that when the crown-gate eye is correct it has complete efficacy (頂門眼正有全功). Dahui says a flash of lightning opens the crown-gate eye (激電爍開頂門眼). In a direct exchange, a monk says the furnace has opened it; the teacher asks what it is, the monk bows, and the teacher strikes him and says, “it has been knocked blind” (擉瞎了也). A transmission record appraises Zhaozhou as possessing it while distinguishing black and white in a stone-struck spark (趙州具頂門眼，向擊石火裏分緇素). The term occurs 276 times in 123 allowlisted files.
Senses.Note: The corpus gives no anatomical account beyond the crown-of-the-head image. Common extensions are “possess the crown-gate eye” (54 hits in 29 files), “open the crown-gate eye” (19/16), “throw open the crown-gate eye” (9/8), and “the correct eye at the crown-gate” (142/85). The longer “one eye at the crown-gate” appears twice. These are recorded as morphology and deployment, not recast as an imported concept.

Occurrences.Kwic: 欲明向上事。須具頂門眼。若具頂門眼。始契出家心。既契出家心。常具頂門眼。要會頂門眼麼。四京人著衣喫飯。兩浙人飽暖自如。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Lushan Wuxiang Fazhen's address says: “To understand the upward matter, one must possess the eye at the crown of the head. If one possesses it, one first accords with the heart of leaving home; having accorded with that heart, one constantly possesses the eye. Do you want to understand it? People in the four capitals dress and eat; people in the two Zhejiang circuits are full and warm.” He is named in the text but absent from the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 據令而行。直得掃蹤滅跡。且道誵訛在什麼處。具頂門眼者。請試舉看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's pointer before Xuansha's case asks where the complication lies and says: “Those who possess the eye at the crown of the head, please try to raise it and see.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 復云。坐見東山振古風。頂門眼正有全功。操持臨濟金剛劍。倜儻楊岐栗棘蓬。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu's verse says: “Seated, see Dongshan stir the ancient wind; when the eye at the crown-gate is correct, it has complete efficacy; wield Linji's diamond sword and Yangqi's chestnut-burr.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道。衲僧有甚麼長處。良久云。激電爍開頂門眼。隔谿猿呌一聲寒。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui asks what strength a patch-robed monk has, pauses, and says: “Flashing lightning opens the eye at the crown of the head; across the stream an ape's cry sounds cold.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「恁麼則豁開頂門眼。」師云：「如何是頂門眼？」僧禮拜，師打，云：「擉瞎了也。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Chaozong's record a monk says, “Then the eye at the crown of the head is thrown open.” The teacher asks, “What is the eye at the crown of the head?” The monk bows; the teacher strikes him and says, “It has been knocked blind.” Chaozong is not in the roster.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師召眾曰。趙州具頂門眼。向擊石火裏分緇素。閃電光中明縱奪。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After raising Zhaozhou's words, the unnamed master under the “lineage heirs of Tianning Zhuo” calls the assembly and says: “Zhaozhou possessed the eye at the crown of the head, distinguishing black and white within a stone-struck spark and making release and capture clear within lightning.” This is a later appraisal of Zhaozhou.
